sector_model: fabless semiconductor: growth, FCF after SBC and net debt; announced stock acquisition adds dilution and regulatory risk
thesis: Marvell Technology (Nasdaq: MRVL), custom AI silicon and data-center connectivity, large cap. FY27 Q2 (to 2026-08-01, 10-Q filed 2026-08-28): revenue 2.739B (+36.5%), GAAP net income 308M (EPS 0.33), cash 3.93B, debt principal 5.00B (no maturities before FY2029; 1.5B revolver undrawn), 876.9M shares. TTM (FY26 10-K + 6M FY27 - 6M FY26): revenue 9.45B, GAAP NI 2.64B (EPS 3.02, includes a large FY26 Q3 profit of 1.90B that I did not trace to a cause), OCF 2.20B, capex 0.47B, FCF 1.73B. At 156.76 (2026-11-13 close, -4.7% on the day, 52-week 70.69-329.88, about 52% below the high) market cap is about 137.6B: 52x TTM GAAP EPS, FCF yield 1.26% (0.65% after 0.83B SBC). The new fact is the all-stock deal to buy Lumentum announced 2026-11-02 (agreement 2026-11-01): 4.500 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, about 115B enterprise value (about 1,132 per share, 23.9% premium to 10-28), Marvell holders to own about 67% of the combined company, expected close first half 2028, outside date 2027-11-01 extendable to 2028-08-01. Marvell would issue roughly 430M shares (about 49% more than today's count; my estimate from the 67/33 split) and pays 5.8B if its board withdraws support, 3.2B regulatory break fee. Stock moved from 171.97 (11-03) to 133.55 (11-05) and 168.80 (11-11). So a growing AI hardware supplier is priced on forward earnings (forward P/E 27.8x per stockanalysis, unverified) while trailing cash yield is thin and the standalone company is about to become a different, larger, less visible one.
counterthesis: Trailing cash yield 1.3% (0.7% after SBC) and 52x GAAP EPS leave no cushion if AI capex slows. The deal is a very large, stock-funded bet: about 49% dilution, 5.8B/3.2B termination exposure, regulatory risk (HSR, China is 42% of revenue by destination so approvals elsewhere may matter), integration of a different business, a 1.5 to 2 year wait with deal uncertainty, and Marvell's own shares are the currency, so a falling share price changes what Lumentum holders receive in value terms. Barron's items cited on stockanalysis tie the recent drop to dilution and merger doubts and a separate report about Nvidia's CEO; I did not verify them. I have not read Lumentum financials, so I cannot judge what is being bought. Customer concentration, custom silicon dependence on a few hyperscalers, and the FY26 one-off profit are unresolved.
invalidation: Evidence for the thesis fails if revenue growth falls well below 20% for two quarters, FCF stays under about 2% of market value while capex rises, or the Lumentum deal terms or approval risk turn out worse than the stock price implies; deal termination would reset the case.
